title: CI: a job ran over 7 minutes
thread:
**Issue #3258 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #3258: CI: a job ran over 7 minutes
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[CI run 42119863917](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42119863917) on `bot/issue-3015` (`95c9821`, pull_request) had jobs over the 7-minute alert (#73):

| Job | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [web (unit 1/4)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42119863917/job/127594383281) | 8m 52s | success |

Split the slow job further until every job finishes under the 5-minute target, not just under the 7-minute alert, so the fix has headroom. Most splits are a count in `scripts/ci-shards.toml` (#3072): `web (unit k/K)`, `e2e smoke (k/K)` (for e2e, also refresh the `WEIGHTS` in `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs`), or a `rust (test <group>)` group, whose count runs its tests in that many jobs, split by name. A count splits the run, not the compile: a group slow to compile needs its tests in more binaries (the engine's `rules_<n>` each get a job by themselves). Anything that cannot be made fast belongs in the daily `.github/workflows/super.yml`, not in CI.

Night bot: you cannot change `.github/`, and a count or a new `rules_<n>` needs no change there. When the split needs a new group or other flags in `.github/ci/rust-test.toml`, or any other change under `.github/`, make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/ci-duration.yml`._

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-3` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42139602695)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`web (unit k/K)` finishes under 5 minutes in every shard. `web (unit 1/4)` took 8m 52s, over the 7-minute alert, and the issue asks for headroom under 5 minutes. The one lever the night bot may use is the shard count in `scripts/ci-shards.toml`, so raise `[web] unit` from 4 to 8. 8 is the generator's maximum (`MAX_SHARDS` in `.github/ci/matrix.py`). Vitest's `--shard=k/K` sorts the test files by a hash of their path and deals them out by count. After the excludes in `ci.yml`, the web, Worker and admin projects hold about 468 test files, so each shard drops from about 117 files to about 59. No count can skip a test.

**One part needs a person:** `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` hard-codes `unit = 4` (see Open questions). The night bot cannot edit `bot/`. Its three tests fail once the count changes, and `bot selftest` then goes red on `main` after the merge.

## Files to touch

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `scripts/ci-shards.toml` | change: `[web]` table, `unit = 4` becomes `unit = 8`, plus a short comment line saying why |

Do not touch:
- `.github/` (the workflow, `matrix.py`, `rust-test.toml`).
- `bot/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`. In particular `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` is the person's part.
- `scripts/ci-scope.sh` and `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`. They treat `scripts/ci-shards.toml` as a file that runs every group, and that stays true.
- `[rust-test]` and `[e2e]`, and `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs`. Neither is slow in this issue.
- Any web test or `vitest.config.ts`.

No spec section or ruling governs the change. It is CI configuration only: no ruling note, no card, no engine code.

## Steps

1. In `scripts/ci-shards.toml`, find the `[web]` table (it has `unit = 4`). Change the value to `unit = 8`. Keep the key `unit` and keep the value a bare integer: `matrix.py` accepts only an int from 1 to 8 and refuses `"8"`, `8.0` and `true`.
2. In the same file, add this comment directly above `[web]`, below the existing `# \`web (unit k/K)\`…` line:
   `# 4 shards ran one past seven minutes (web (unit 1/4), 8m 52s, #3258); 8 is the most a count may be (matrix.py's MAX_SHARDS).`
   Change nothing else in the file: no reformatting, and no change to the `[rust-test]` or `[e2e]` counts.
3. Run `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py matrix | grep web_unit_shards`. It must print `web_unit_shards=[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8]`. Run `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py matrix | tail -n 3` too. It lists the job counts, and `rust_test` and `e2e_smoke_shards` must be unchanged. That proves the generator accepts the file.
4. Run `cd bot && python3 -m unittest tests.test_ci_matrix`, then `cd ..` back to the repository root. Expect exactly three failures, all from the hard-coded 4 and the person's part:
   - `test_the_committed_files_give_todays_jobs`
   - `test_the_web_and_e2e_counts_come_from_the_file`
   - `test_it_refuses_what_could_hide_a_job_or_flood_the_runners`

   Every other test in that file must pass. Do **not** edit the test file, and do not set `unit` back to 4 to quiet it. Put these three failures, and the cause, in the final report.

## Tests

The change is configuration, so no new test is written. A web or Rust test cannot prove a CI timing, and the one test that holds the counts lives under `bot/`.

- `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py matrix` (step 3) is the proof the new count is valid.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` still passes. It holds `scripts/ci-shards.toml` to the Rust groups and does not read the count. Run it only if `pnpm install` has been done.
- The harness's own checks run unchanged.
- The proof that every shard is under 5 minutes is the next CI run on the pull request. `scripts/ci-scope.sh` runs every web job for a change to this file, so `web (unit 1/8)` to `web (unit 8/8)` appear and are timed there. The builder cannot measure it and must not claim the target is met.

## Done when

- [ ] `scripts/ci-shards.toml` holds `unit = 8` under `[web]` and the comment, and nothing else in it changed.
- [ ] `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py matrix` prints `web_unit_shards=[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8]`.
- [ ] The final report lists the three `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` failures by name, says the lines are the person's, and says `bot selftest` is skipped on this pull request but runs on `main` after the merge.
- [ ] The report says plainly that the under-5-minutes target is unverified until the first CI run with 8 shards.
- [ ] The harness's checks pass: rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests, web tests. Nothing under `.github/`, `bot/`, `.harness/` or `.squishy/` is changed.

## Risks

- **Red `bot selftest` on `main`.** `ci.yml`'s `bot` scope ignores `scripts/ci-shards.toml`, so this pull request and its merge-queue run skip `bot selftest` and pass. The push to `main` runs everything, and `test_ci_matrix.py` then fails. Mitigation: the person's four-line edit below, ideally pushed to this branch before it merges. The builder only reports it, since it may not edit `bot/`.
- **8 may still not reach 5 minutes.**
  - Each shard keeps a fixed cost: checkout, `pnpm install`, the `web-build` artifact download and unpack. A count only halves the vitest work.
  - Hash-dealing can leave a heavy file together with others.
  - No per-file timings were available (the planning session had no installed dependencies and no network), so this is unmeasured.
  - If a shard is still over 5 minutes after the next run, the follow-ups are a person's. Either raise `MAX_SHARDS` in `.github/ci/matrix.py` and `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py`, or move the slowest files to the daily run through `apps/web/src/test/daily.ts`, with per-file timings in hand.
  - The script-driven tests (`apps/admin/build.test.ts` runs real Vite builds, and `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`, `server-image.test.ts`, `build-wasm-cache.test.ts` and `deploy-rehearsal.test.ts` run scripts) are the likely heavy ones. They guard CI and deploys, so they were not moved or skipped here.
- **Runner load.** 8 jobs instead of 4 cost 4 more runners per pull request. 8 is the cap the repository chose for that reason.
- No determinism, replay, hidden-information or crate-README contract is touched.

## Open questions

For a person (the part the night bot may not do):

1. **`bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py`**, to change with this pull request:
   - line 73: `self.assertEqual(out["web_unit_shards"], [1, 2, 3, 4])` becomes `self.assertEqual(out["web_unit_shards"], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8])`
   - line 118: `self.repo.edit(matrix.COUNTS, "unit = 4", "unit = 5")` becomes `self.repo.edit(matrix.COUNTS, "unit = 8", "unit = 5")`. The expected `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` on line 121 stays.
   - line 131: `("unit = 4", "unit = 0", "from 1 to 8"),` becomes `("unit = 8", "unit = 0", "from 1 to 8"),`
   - line 132: `("unit = 4", "units = 4", "holds only `unit`"),` becomes `("unit = 8", "units = 8", "holds only `unit`"),`

   Land it on this branch before the pull request merges if you can. If not, land it straight after, so `main`'s `bot selftest` is not left red.
2. **Optional, cosmetic, under `.github/`:** `ci.yml` line 24 ("in quarters") and line 955 ("In quarters, by file") now read wrongly. Change them to "in eighths" or "in shards (scripts/ci-shards.toml)".
<!-- /jackioh-bot:plan -->
```
